# Scheduling benchmark (generated by scripts/run_benchmark.py)

Simulated schedules on Observed topology and labor data. 306 instances = 46 circuits × damage sets (Observed Feb-2025 records, plus seeded Poisson draws at 1×) × crew counts {1, calibrated default, 2× default}. Every policy sees identical tasks, hours and crews. Metric: customer-outage hours (Σ customers × hours until service, each premise counted once; service returns only when every damaged zone on the path is repaired). 'Reduction' is 1 − ours/baseline; negative = we lost. Swap pass budget 0.5 s per instance.

### Solver status

- Swap-improvement pass: ran on 306 instances, mean gain 1.39% (max 20.42%), runtime per dependency-aware solve mean 0.06 s, max 0.50 s.
- Exact reference (≤ 7 tasks, brute force over all orders): 64 instances; mean gap 0.19%, max gap 9.15%, instances at the optimum 60.
- With several crews the ordering is list-scheduled and therefore a heuristic; optimality holds only for one crew.

### Scale sanity check (not a fit)

With the calibrated default crews and the Observed Feb-2025 damage sets, the dependency-aware schedule restores the last customer after a median of 2.7 days (10th–90th percentile 1.8–3.0 days). The organizer's day-granularity repair records for that storm show report→repair gaps of 0–6 days for 97% of records. The crew default was calibrated to a 72 h FIFO makespan, so this agreement is partly by construction; it is a scale check, not validation.
